title: Skill-Based Resonance Recognition
opening: Skills shape what you notice and what you can do. Combining them may open an opportunity in a new setting, but the target field still sets what must be checked.

labels.comparisonIntro: One person has coached beginners and written technical instructions. Those skills could help them improve a software lesson. Do they also let the person judge whether the software is secure?
labels.pair: Coaching reveals where learners pause; technical writing can make the next step clear.
labels.tutorialTransfer: Coaching may reveal where a learner gets stuck. Technical writing may help explain the next step.
labels.tutorialBoundary: A software practitioner still checks that commands, prerequisites and technical facts are correct.
labels.securityTransfer: The pair may help explain a procedure or reveal where readers get lost.
labels.securityBoundary: Neither skill establishes that a system is secure. A security specialist checks the design.
labels.targetPrompt: Which target are you reasoning about?
labels.tutorialPrompt: The pair may improve the teaching transition. A software practitioner still checks the technical content.
labels.securityPrompt: The pair may improve the explanation, but it cannot certify the security design. Ask a security specialist to check it.
labels.unknownPrompt: Keep the boundary open until target work shows what the pair can reliably do.
labels.practiceTitle: Try a pair of your skills
labels.practiceIntro: Choose two skills you actually use and a possible setting outside their familiar application. Keep a useful pattern separate from expertise you have not established.
labels.private: This optional private draft is separate from the six required assessment questions.
labels.needAnswer: Add at least one part of your own skill combination before saving.
labels.oversize: This full draft is over 2,000 characters. Shorten it to save; all of your text remains on screen.
labels.sourceExcerpt: List a few skills and the patterns each helps you notice. Examine combinations: what might one skill reveal that another lets you act on? Identify an opportunity to investigate outside the skill’s familiar application.
